newsitem.title: USA: NYS Teachers keep tobacco stocks underweighted.
newsitem.headline: NYS Teachers keep tobacco stocks underweighted.

text.p: The $58 billion New York State Teachers' Retirement System (NYSTRS) said that its board had decided to maintain its underweighting of tobacco stocks as a result of a string of recent, important rulings by judges.

"The NYSTRS will maintain an underweighted exposure in the tobacco sector of its Russell 3000 by up to 25 percent of its representation in the index," said the fund, in prepared remarks. The fund has about $26 billion invested in the index, said Bob DeLuca, director of member and employee relations.
"We have approximately $565 million worth of tobacco stock," DeLuca said.
He said the board, which adopted the tobacco policy in April 1996, made the decision to keep the restriction at its meeting on April 29.

In a prepared statement, the fund said it would vote in favor of reasonable proxy proposals directed at spinning off non-tobacco-related components. It also plans to stay in contact with tobacco companies and try to persuade them to reduce their potential exposure, by taking measures such as curbing the marketing of tobacco products to minors.

The board said its policy was evolving. "The retirement board and staff continue to monitor tobacco companies and related issues on an ongoing basis and may take further action consistent with the board's long-term fiduciary responsibilities," it said.
